topic: Rapid-MLX DSH Provider: Configure DeepSeek Harness to Run on Native Apple Silicon via Rapid-MLX

key_points: Official Rapid-MLX guide: run DeepSeek Harness against a local Rapid-MLX server via the generic openai-completions provider (never impersonate deepseek-official)
DSH is a Tier-1 release-gate agent for Rapid-MLX: every version bump runs dsh through a real multi-step bug-fix task against a local 35B model
Tracks @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.0-rc.7 (verified 2026-08-17); rc.6->rc.7 did not change the provider schema
Setup: npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh; rapid-mlx serve qwen3.5-9b-4bit; rapid-mlx agents dsh --setup; then dsh web or dsh --profile headless
--setup auto-writes $DSH_HOME/settings.yaml (~/.dsh/settings.yaml) preserving unrelated providers, backup, atomic write; refuses to overwrite a file changed after the preview

Uses RAPID_MLX_API_KEY=not-needed sentinel in .credentials.yaml (generic OpenAI transport requires a credential reference even for unauthenticated localhost); existing values preserved, values redacted in preview
Requires Node 22.15+ (DSH imports Node Zstd stream API but does not declare it; mismatch reported before opaque plugin-loader stack trace)
Test with rapid-mlx agents dsh --test (isolated DSH_HOME + workspace)
DeepSeek Harness (dsh) official site — DeepSeek's open-source agent harness in developer preview
Positioned as 'Everything is a plugin' — CLI, web UI, tools, slash commands, skills, MCP all plugins
Developer preview means compatibility-breaking changes expected as framework iterates
DeepSeek-Harness (dsh) is DeepSeek's open-source agent harness where every feature is a plugin (plugin version 0.1.0-rc.5 at time of writing)
Built on a general-purpose Cordis plugin framework; no separate manifest per capability type
Explains plugin architecture: tools, commands, skills, MCP all collapse into one plugin mechanism
Apple's MLX — an array framework for Apple silicon (28k+ stars)
The underlying tensor framework that Rapid-MLX builds on for native Apple Silicon inference
Foundation for why Rapid-MLX can outperform llama.cpp/Ollama on M-series Macs
Rapid-MLX throughput vs Ollama: 558 vs 250 t/s (gpt-oss), 460 vs 277 (Qwen), 172 vs 96 (Gemma)
Up to 3x Ollama's throughput measured; 82.9 t/s on Qwen3 at 8-stream continuous batching
2x, 1.5x, 1.33x faster in various configs; 390ms TTFT on warm cached runs
Continuous batching helps Rapid-MLX while others degrade from 4 to 8 streams

stats.fact: Rapid-MLX is 'the fastest local AI engine for Apple Silicon' — measured up to 3x Ollama's throughput (558 vs 250 t/s on gpt-oss; 460 vs 277 on Qwen; 172 vs 96 on Gemma).
Rapid-MLX achieves 82.9 t/s on Qwen at 8-stream with continuous batching, while competing engines degrade from 4 to 8 streams.
DeepSeek Harness (deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) is a TypeScript open-source agent harness with ~204k GitHub stars, currently in developer preview (0.1.0-rc.7 tracked by Rapid-MLX).
Apple's MLX framework (ml-explore/mlx) has 28k+ GitHub stars and is the Apple Silicon tensor foundation Rapid-MLX is built on.

Rapid-MLX supports 17 tool parsers, prompt cache, reasoning separation, cloud routing, and is a drop-in OpenAI/Anthropic replacement working with Claude Code, Cursor, Aider, Hermes, Codex, and DeepSeek Harness.
DeepSeek Harness requires Node 22.15+ because it imports Node's Zstd stream API but does not declare the minimum in its npm manifest.
Rapid-MLX install: 'brew install rapid-mlx' or the guided installer 'curl -fsSL https://rapidmlx.com/install.sh | bash'; both install the rapid-mlx CLI.
Serve an OpenAI-compatible endpoint with 'rapid-mlx serve qwen3.5-9b-4bit' bound to http://localhost:8000 (/v1 for OpenAI route; /v1/messages for Anthropic).

angles: Run DeepSeek Harness 100% locally on Apple Silicon — no cloud API keys, no data leaving the Mac, using a drop-in OpenAI-compatible provider.
Why you should use the generic openai-completions provider instead of deepseek-official for a local endpoint (avoid fake API keys + fake model contracts).
The one-command setup: rapid-mlx agents dsh --setup auto-writes $DSH_HOME/settings.yaml preserving your existing providers.
Rapid-MLX is a Tier-1 release-gate agent for Rapid-MLX — production-grade verified compatibility.
Cost/performance: MLX-powered inference is dramatically faster than Ollama on M-series chips, so your local DeepSeek harness agent loop feels snappy.
Node 22.15+ gotcha and the exit-0 trap (dsh returns 0 even when a task fails — assert on output, not exit status).
